decisions.reason: “Even” preserves the emphasis of 마저 as the music fades too.
The uncertainty is retained in the following line, so the standalone repetition can go.
SOL folds the uncertainty into the question while keeping both possible sounds.
The source says the nod was all he could offer; SOL drops that limitation.
“Ended in victory” preserves the source’s explicit victory before the feast.
The repeated phrasing preserves her being both alone and apart from everyone.
“Change hands” adds a change of ownership absent from the image of mountains and rivers changing.
“Those who survived” keeps the meaning and reads naturally.
SOL adds that the time was shared together; the source only says it might be their last.
“Memorial rite” keeps the sense of a ceremony honoring the dead.
The source explicitly has him part his lips; SOL removes that small physical action.
The source refers to fleeting emotions, not fleeting moments.
“Come to me” preserves the approach and keeps the sense of someone staying beside her.
The source says she, too, had guessed why he came; SOL drops “too.”
SOL keeps the penetrating gaze and the pause to steady his breathing.
“Fired the first shot” retains the source’s signal-shot image; SOL reduces it to signaling.
The revised pronouns and phrasing preserve the defeat, pursuit, and delayed reinforcements.
“Unknown man” keeps the sense that his identity was not known.
The reinforcements saw everything, not merely proof of what happened.
The possessive construction keeps the same title and makes the generation reference clear.
The split sentence preserves the announcement and the news spreading through the realm.
The recast retains the repeated divisions and reunifications before their unification.
SOL keeps the admiration for his achievements without changing the sense.
The stars still echo her title against the vast heavens, preserving the comparison.
The source calls him a being like a miracle; SOL turns the person into “a miracle.”
The source marks a sudden parting of his lips; SOL omits that beat.
“Slid slowly down from the sky to me” preserves the direction of her gaze.
“A fraction too late” keeps the slight delay.
The source emphasizes that her eyes wavered only imperceptibly; SOL drops that degree.
“Kept the question to myself” preserves the decision to conceal it.
The recast keeps her point that greater closeness would not make her account different.
“Fleeting hint of agitation” preserves the brief disturbance before her calm reply.
“That is why we stand here together now” keeps the stated reason they are facing one another.
The reordered sentences preserve that her decades of wandering support her words.
SOL changes a path too difficult for him to judge into one harder than his own.
“To my mind” keeps the narrator’s view that her answer is true yet incomplete.
The recast preserves instinct and cold reason leading to the same conclusion.
The split phrasing keeps their shared life-and-death experiences and her distance from the group.
“What he had told me” preserves the Slaughter Saint’s account without changing the event.
“Several times” matches the source’s repeated reconsideration without adding an uncountable exaggeration.
The hypothetical is that he would have acted; SOL shifts it to the indicative “I acted.”
“Surrounding Xining” preserves the source’s battle around the city; “around” is less precise.
“On every side” keeps the image of deaths in all directions.
“On the strength of” naturally preserves her reliance on the old letter.
“Swallowed a breath” matches the source’s 숨을 삼키다.
The source stresses that the water surged forcefully; SOL drops that intensity.
“Into my leather shoes” preserves the cold entering them, and the shortened thought transition remains clear.
The source says the eyes were watching him intently; “watchful” does not retain that focused gaze.
The pronoun has a clear referent, so omitting the repeated title does not lose the Korean sense.
The source says she answered at once; SOL removes the immediacy.
“Not a trace” keeps the absence of both lies and ill will.
“Those few words” preserves the brief phrase and its continued echo.
“Helped a great deal” preserves the extent of his gratitude in natural English.
